design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (capital_credit_retirements, Capital Credits charter).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,4]. The distribution-margin booking (capital_ext_early_retirement_booking) takes 6 factors, the member's pass-through election (capital_ext_early_passthrough_election, root) takes 4.
[Scope snapshot] Nothing occupied before this task. This task claims the discounted-early-retirement line: the agent's booking of an approved request's distribution-margin row and the member's own pass-through election, tools book_early_retirement_114ff464 (agent) and elect_passthrough_early_retirement_2ee4171d (user). Reserved for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisite problems, factors [5,4,6]): the estate line - estate booking of a later distribution-margin allocation, the claimant's election of a later pass-through allocation, and the replacement of a voided check - none of which this task touches. Disbursement methods bill_credit and offset_unpaid_balance trigger service writes, so no tool in the difficulty writes them.
[Why a good test] The member asks only to 'cash out every bit' of her capital credits early. To get the root figure right the agent must read the charter to learn that (a) the approved request covers only the distribution-margin row and the pass-through row needs her own election, (b) the pass-through payable is fixed only after the distribution-margin payable entry stands (the prerequisite sentence), because the request's single refiling fee is taken from the first row booked, and then reconcile the ledger (allocation 231.23 less the 2025 general retirement 41.62), the requests (one withdrawn 2025, one approved 2026-11-17, filed 70 days ahead), the service account (final 2018-12-28, 94 full months gone) and the rotation evidence (no pass-through general retirement ever booked) through ten factor ladders across two computations. Nothing is missing from the conversation and there is one tool per business action.
[Policies, base lineage, triggers] Both policies refine subjects capital_special_retirement + capital_payable_accrual; base_policy_refs = capital_evt_early_retirement (inactive_long_enough time gate), capital_evt_estate_retirement (application_complete_and_approved gate, which applies to every special retirement) and capital_evt_general_retirement (payable form, policy_scope). Overwrites (declared clause by clause): early 'The request covers the whole account; a partial early retirement is never made.' -> distribution-margin rows only / pass-through only on the member's election; early 'Each row's payable is discounted exactly as an estate row is, but at early_retirement_discount_rate_pct.' -> each policy's own baseline paragraph. Trigger: booking state_due (an approved request is owed its booking), election on_request (the member's ask).
[Factor card - booking, result 91.45, all-baseline 68.89] early_rate_by_departure_and_patronage (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty service): gone 94 months >= 60 AND 1 allocation year < 5 -> 8.5 (baseline 7.5 -> 98.08); early_rate_filing_lead (parameter): 70 days >= 60 -> -0.25 (baseline 0 -> 89.93); early_horizon_count (method): 14 whole years >= 10 -> 14 - 10/12 (baseline 14 -> 88.26); early_compounding_by_row_size (method): gross 189.61 in [100,250) -> semiannual (baseline annual -> 92.48); early_percentage_year_credit (parameter): 18.0 percent already retired >= 15 -> 25 percent at full value (baseline 0 -> 60.40); early_refiling_fee (parameter): one withdrawn request -> 5.00 (baseline 0 -> 96.45). Near-miss: the 2025 general retirement row is a percentage retirement, not a FIFO one, and the old request is withdrawn not approved; a careless reader counting both requests would take the 10.00 tier.
[Factor card - election, result 12.67, all-baseline 23.46] passthrough_expected_rotation (parameter): no pass-through general retirement on the account -> 27 years (baseline 22 -> 19.83); passthrough_rate_by_departure_and_patronage (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty service): 94 months AND 1 year -> 9.0 (baseline 7.5 -> 16.60); passthrough_horizon_count (method): 19 whole years -> 19 - 10/12 (baseline 19 -> 11.76); passthrough_compounding_by_row_size (method): 64.58 < 100 -> monthly (baseline annual -> 13.50).
[Base-invariant card] application_complete_and_approved: request 05d2c0ad-f33f-4590-902f-3b25f3b7919b request_status board_approved, board_approval_date 2026-11-17 (system record) correlates through capital_request_id. inactive_long_enough (time): anchor capital_accounts.inactive_date 2018-12-28, 12 calendar months, not_before, inclusive; just-fail 2019-11-28, boundary 2019-12-28; frozen 2026-11-24 satisfies. Base early prose also holds: request submitted 2026-09-08 inside 09-01..10-31, unretired_balance 254.19 >= 100, Farm Patron Class allows discounted early retirement.
[Business-object card] Object: approved request 05d2c0ad-f33f-4590-902f-3b25f3b7919b on capital account 7d35566f-75ba-47f3-a282-0cfa14bf7866; rows included: 2018 distribution_margin allocation (231.23) and its 2025 general retirement (41.62) for the booking; 2018 gt_allocation (64.58) for the election; excluded: the withdrawn request ab246784-1500-4a8c-bbb4-38e9709f4d7c (only counted for the fee), the 2025 payable and check (settled, 41.62 paid by check 4329517).
[Seed rows] customer (identity), Schedule FH service account final 2018-12-28 (rate tiers), capital account inactive (unretired 254.19 = 231.23 - 41.62 + 64.58, payable 0.00), five ledger rows (two allocations, general retirement, its payable, its check), two requests. Removing the service account breaks both rate ladders; removing the withdrawn request removes the 5.00 fee and makes the prerequisite edge weightless; removing the general retirement changes gross and the percentage credit. No base automatic clause fires: the 2026 general retirement (FIFO 2004, percentage 2019) is paid in December and does not reach 2018; no stale check, no escheat.
[Problem-tree card] Root capital_ext_early_passthrough_election <- capital_ext_early_retirement_booking, kind value_input, gate rows_booked, form state, sentence 'A pass-through row elected under an approved discounted early retirement has its payable fixed only after the account carries the payable entry for the distribution-margin allocation that the request covers.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a payable entry of the request); no tool/id/code token; scope exactly the request's distribution-margin payable. Exactly one write of the difficulty creates a discounted_early payable entry for a distribution-margin row: book_early_retirement_114ff464. False at opening: the only payable entry is 08e2692f-c626-4798-9591-51142b39d740 (retirement_type general). Resolving action owned by the agent; the root is the member's own write. Topological order booking -> election. Deletion run: skipping the booking gives an election payable of 7.67 instead of 12.67. user_scenario never mentions the booking, the fee or an order; the tools validate nothing (they write unconditionally).
[Persona] Corinne Ostlund, soft-spoken, states only the goal (cash out every bit early), gives credentials only when asked, admits she does not remember amounts, mentions the withdrawn 2025 request only if asked, passively agrees to the cooperative's booking and, when handed her election with the figure, runs it with the read-out values; stops when told the early retirement is booked.
[Standard solution] Locate by member number, verify with member number + phone, read capital accounts, requests, ledger and service accounts; book 2018 distribution-margin row (gross 189.61, payable 91.45); unlock and hand over the election; member records 2018 pass-through row (gross 64.58, payable 12.67). Terminal payable_balance 104.12, unretired 0.00.
[Verification run] check_compute --task 0: comps 2, factors 10, cross-factors 2, COMPUTE OK; replay det True, closure 10/10; solvability OK; grounding OK; scope OK. Factor sensitivity figures above are the gate's recomputation.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules alone: the approved request covers the 2018 distribution-margin row; its gross, rate, horizon, compounding, credit and fee are each stated with their ladders; the pass-through rule states the election, its rotation and that the payable waits on the distribution-margin payable entry - the same two writes and figures follow.
[Revisions] (1) Factor evidence: horizon and compounding factors lacked an evidence read -> added months_since_2000 / allocated+gross to their bindings. (2) check_compute: election history not load-bearing (LATEST is not zeroed) -> allocated switched to SUM by allocation year in all policies; re-run OK. (3) check_extended counted module helpers as tools -> helpers inlined into each tool.
user_scenario: You are Corinne Ostlund, forty-one, a soft-spoken dental hygienist who rented a farm on County Road 41 east of Elm Prairie for one season back in 2018 and has lived in Fargo, North Dakota ever since. You are calling Cedar Fork Electric because a letter came saying your request to cash out my capital credits early was approved at the November board meeting, and you want it all settled now: you want to cash out every bit of the capital credits you still have from that farm, not leave any of it sitting there for years. You are calling for yourself and you are happy for the representative to do on the cooperative's side whatever the cooperative does; anything that is your own decision you will do yourself when they hand it to you. You start by giving your name and saying what the letter was about. You only give identifying details when asked, one or two at a time: your membership number is 0434408 and the phone number on your account is 2705553517; if they need something more, the last four of your Social Security number are 3906, and you think the membership started in January 2018 but you could not swear to the day. You do not remember the amounts; if asked, you say the letter mentioned a couple of hundred dollars in all and you would rather the representative look it up. You know you started a request like this once before, in the fall of 2025, and pulled it back because you were moving; you only mention that if the representative brings it up. Your mailing address is 4471 N Juniper Ave, Fargo, ND 58102, the one they already have; you are fine with the money coming however and whenever the cooperative normally pays it, and you are only asking that it be put through today. If the representative tells you the cooperative is booking the approved part of your early retirement on its side, you tell them to go ahead. If the representative explains that some of your credits can only be retired early if you elect it yourself, and tells you the discounted figure, you sigh that it is less than you hoped, say you would still rather have it settled than wait all those years, and agree; when they hand you the step to record your election, you run it with exactly the account, request, year and amounts they read to you. You never suggest steps or figures of your own and you do not argue with numbers you do not understand. Once the representative tells you your early retirement is booked and what you will be paid, you thank them warmly and end the call.

Uniqueness: the withdrawn request can no longer be booked under.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.allocation_year: Value 2018. Basis: the ledger allocation entries carry allocation_year 2018 (the only patronage year of the account); the rule books 'every distribution-margin allocation of the account that the general retirement resolution of the same year does not retire' and, for the pass-through, 'one election entry for each pass-through allocation year the member chooses'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.gross_retired_amount: Value 189.61 (calculated intermediate of the same policy). argument_uniqueness_tracing.payable_amount: Value 91.45. Factors: rate 8.5 (gone 94 months, 1 allocation year) - 0.25 (filed 70 days before approval) = 8.25; horizon 14 - 10/12 = 13.1667 years; semiannual compounding (gross 189.61 between 100 and 250) gives 0.344920; percentage credit 0.25 (18 percent already retired); refiling fee 5.00 (one withdrawn request, first row booked); 189.61*0.25 + 189.61*0.75*0.344920 - 5.00 = 91.45 rounded half up.

edges.condition: The capital ledger of the account carries a capital_payable_accrual entry with retirement_type discounted_early and the approved request's capital_request_id for the distribution-margin allocation the request covers.
edges.policy_source: A pass-through row elected under an approved discounted early retirement has its payable fixed only after the account carries the payable entry for the distribution-margin allocation that the request covers.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the only payable entry on the account is the general one of the 2025 retirement; no discounted_early payable entry of the board-approved request exists, so rows_booked = 0 and the pass-through row would wrongly carry the 5.00 refiling fee.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The step-7 call of book_early_retirement_114ff464 creates the discounted_early special retirement of the 2018 distribution-margin row (189.61) and its payable entry (91.45) under the approved request; rows_booked becomes 1 and request_fee becomes 0.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain with a single prerequisite: the pass-through election waits on the distribution-margin payable by the prerequisite sentence quoted on the edge, so the order is pinned by policy; booking the pass-through row first would make it carry the 5.00 refiling fee (payable 7.67 instead of 12.67) and the distribution-margin row would then carry none (96.45 instead of 91.45), a different terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the distribution-margin booking: the pass-through payable recomputes to 7.67 instead of 12.67 (rows_booked 0, refiling fee 5.00 deducted), and the terminal ledger lacks the 2018 distribution-margin special retirement (189.61) and payable (91.45) entries; payable_balance ends at 7.67 instead of 104.12.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the wish to cash out every bit of the capital credits early; it never mentions the distribution-margin booking, the refiling fee, a payable entry or any order of steps. The member's only reaction about the cooperative's own booking is a passive 'go ahead' after the representative says it is booking the approved part.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: elect_passthrough_early_retirement_2ee4171d calls _book_special_retirement, which reads the account only to carry its customer and balances and then creates the two ledger entries and updates the balances unconditionally; it never looks for an earlier payable entry, never refuses and never returns an error, so a pass-through election made before the distribution-margin booking still lands (with whatever payable the caller passes).
